subject: Premium SLA options for BrightNav — availability bands, credits and escalation
messages:
From: Samuel Green <samuel.green@brightnav.com>
To: Dylan Brooks <dylan.brooks@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Mon, 12 Jan 2026 08:15:00 -0800
Subject: Premium SLA for BrightNav — availability, credits and oncall

Hi Dylan,

Thanks for taking a look at this. We're evaluating premium support and SLA options for BrightNav as we prepare to go live with our predictive analytics feature in Q2. Two quick asks so we can scope internal approvals: 

1) Can you sketch the price delta and credits between 99.9% and 99.95% availability tiers (monthly commit + overage)?
2) What would a 1-hour critical-response offering look like vs the standard 4-hour response window (retainer/credits/coverage hours)?

We're on a fairly tight procurement window — aiming to finalize by Feb 5 — and I'll need a clear playbook for escalation coverage (who's oncall, how many handoffs, region considerations). Also want to understand if there's room for an early-commit discount if we sign a 12-month reserved capacity commitment.

Happy to hop on a short call this week. Could you send a concise proposal and the related MAAs?

Thanks,
Samuel
Samuel Green
Head of Infrastructure
BrightNav

P: +1 415-555-0147
From: Dylan Brooks <dylan.brooks@redwoodinference.com>
To: Samuel Green <samuel.green@brightnav.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Mon, 12 Jan 2026 11:40:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Premium SLA for BrightNav — availability, credits and oncall

Hi Samuel — thanks for the clear ask. I put together two concise options and attached a draft SLA + Master Agreement Addendum (MAA) for your procurement team (attached: SLA_Proposal_BrightNav_v2.pdf, MAA-BrightNav.xlsx). Summary below — happy to jump on a 30-minute call tomorrow to walk through.

Option A — Premium (recommended)
- Availability: 99.95% monthly
- Response: 1-hour critical triage (critical incidents only), 4-hour standard for P1
- Credits: 10% monthly credit for availability breach between 99.9–99.95; 25% credit for <99.9
- Retainer: $5k/mo for 24/7 critical oncall (covers up to 4 incidents/mo), additional incidents billed at hourly rate
- Committed reserved capacity: 250k tokens/day equivalent baseline (discounted unit rate)
- Early-commit incentive: 8% uplift discount on total service fee for 12-month prepay

Option B — Standard Uplift
- Availability: 99.9% monthly
- Response: 4-hour P1, business-hours for P2/P3
- Credits: 5% credit for availability below 99.9
- Lower retainer: $2k/mo for extended hours oncall coverage

Notes / tradeoffs:
- The primary cost driver between the tiers is the dedicated oncall retainer + guaranteed capacity. 99.95 requires higher reserved pool and faster escalation paths (hot handoffs).
- If BrightNav can commit to a 12-month reserved capacity minimum, we can tighten the credits matrix and extend the early-commit incentive to 10% (finance-approved conditional).

Next steps:
- I'll schedule a 30-minute call with Marissa (legal) and Karthik (pricing) to align on contract points and the concession guardrails. Could you share your procurement contact and any internal SLA exceptions we should be aware of?

Attachments: SLA_Proposal_BrightNav_v2.pdf (proposal + credits matrix), MAA-BrightNav.xlsx (redline-friendly addendum)

—
Dylan Brooks
Account Executive, Strategic Accounts
Redwood Inference
d: +1 206-555-0132 | m: +1 206-555-9982
From: Dylan Brooks <dylan.brooks@redwoodinference.com>
To: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwoodinference.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Tue, 13 Jan 2026 09:05:00 -0800
Subject: BrightNav — negotiation plan and concession ask (need quick numbers)

Karthik / Marissa —

Looping you in on BrightNav (Samuel Green). They asked for a clear delta between 99.9 and 99.95 and want to know if there's an early-commit discount for 12 months reserved capacity. Procurement timeline: decision target Feb 5.

Key constraints from the customer:
- Wants 1-hour critical-response for true P0s (they consider predictive outages high-impact)
- Open to a 12-month commit if discounts offset retainer
- Sensitive to credits exposure (they will push to narrow our credit band)

My ask: can we provide a defensible concession that I can present on a call this week? Specifically: 
- If they commit 12 months at >= $150k TCV, what's the maximum early-commit discount we can offer on the Premium tier? (Finance guardrails)
- Can we allow a temporary trial of the 1-hour SLA for first 60 days with a punchlist of requirements (observability hooks + runbook) instead of full 24/7 retainer?

Proposed starting position (my recommendation):
- Offer 8% early-commit discount for 12-month commit at $150k TCV
- Hold to credits matrix in the attached proposal, but reduce the 99.95->99.9 credit from 10% -> 8% if customer signs the commit
- Trial 60-day 1-hour critical response as a paid POC: $7k one-time activation + standard retainer after trial if they keep it

Marissa — can you confirm if the temporary POC activation approach is viable from legal/contracting perspective (we'd want a limited-scope addendum)?

I'll run this as our 'call script' if we get a procurement call this week.

Thanks —
Dylan
From: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwoodinference.com>
To: Dylan Brooks <dylan_brooks@redwoodinference.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Thu, 15 Jan 2026 15:02:00 -0800
Subject: Re: BrightNav — negotiation plan and concession ask (need quick numbers)

Dylan —

I spoke with finance and pricing. Here's an actionable concession package you can offer on the call. Call it a structured concession (we keep control gates).

1) Early-commit discount
- 10% off premium service fee if BrightNav commits 12 months and TCV >= $175k (we can stretch to $150k at 8%)

2) Credits tweak
- Keep the baseline credits in your proposal. Offer a 2% additional reduction on the 99.95->99.9 credit band if they sign within the procurement window (effectively 8% v 10%). This is reversible if usage baseline drifts > 25% in a quarter.

3) 1-hour critical-response trial (POC)
- Approve a 60-day trial for a single geography (US-west) at $7k activation + one-time operational readiness checklist (observability + playbook). After trial: convert to full retainer at $5k/mo or revert. Trial includes up to 3 critical incidents; excess incidents billed at published hourly rate.

4) Escalation and handoffs
- Offer a named escalation engineer during business hours and an on-call rotation for nights (regional handoff). Add a clause in MAA limiting liability for third-party infra outages (cloud provider incidents).

Please bind the offer with clear acceptance criteria and an expiry date (we usually do 14 days). Also copy finance-ops on the signed MAA so we can honor the 10% cap and set up billing workflows.

Good to go — call me if they push for deeper credits.

Best,
Karthik Iyer
Head of Pricing & Commercial Operations
Redwood Inference
